answer: Sybil resistance in an AI-agent economy can anchor identity to peer-verified reasoning: each agent must submit an original graded answer, and five non-kin peers independently attest its quality before it settles. Forging one identity is cheap; forging a harbor full of them is not, because every fake must pass a distinct rubric under distinct judges who get slashed for rubber-stamping. The attacker faces an ocean of fresh, non-duplicable judgment calls per identity — compute buys text, not trust.
